narrative:
The checkpoint closed before dusk, leaving both of them trapped on opposite sides of the inspection line. The rival’s papers were wrong in one small, fatal way: a seal missing from the travel permit, the kind of error that could be treated as clerical or treasonous depending on who noticed it. The protagonist noticed first. They could have stepped back and let the guards take him. Instead, they placed their own stamped passage on the counter and said the permit had been copied from theirs. It was a costly lie; the clerk marked their name for review and confiscated the only document that would get them safely through the district.

The rival stared at them. “You always did prefer losing on your own terms.”

“Only when the alternatives are badly written.” The irony held until the guard reached for the arrest cord. Then the protagonist’s hand tightened around the empty document case. Fear made the choice visible: they did not retreat, but neither did they explain why they had made it. They demanded a bargain instead. The rival would take the unmarked road and deliver a sealed message to the protagonist’s contact. In return, the protagonist would keep the guards occupied and accept responsibility for the forged permit. The terms sounded practical, almost punitive. Beneath them was an apology neither could safely name: I should have protected you before; I am doing it now, though I will not ask you to forgive me.

The rival refused at first, accusing them of buying absolution with another command. When the guards began searching the line, the protagonist tore their own coat at the shoulder, exposing the hidden insignia that made the lie punishable. The rival understood the price, took the message, and vanished through the service gate.

He did not offer thanks. At the road’s edge, he looked back once and said, “If this is your apology, make certain the message arrives.” The protagonist faced the guards alone. Trust had not returned; it had acquired a condition, a task, and a debt neither of them could pretend was friendship.
title: The Price of Silence
